---
title: "Hostile text: Python"
jupyter: python3
---

Data and printed text full of characters that mean something to Markdown,
LaTeX, HTML or Quarto. Each must come out literally, wherever it appears,
and nothing printed may change kind because of what it looks like.

```{python}
import pandas as pd

nasty = [
    "$5 and $10", "50% off", "a & b", "#hashtag", "{braces}", "~tilde", "x^2",
    r"C:\path\to\file", "a|b|c", "*stars*", "**bold**", "_under_", "<b>tag</b>",
    "`code`", "@cite", "[link](http://x.y)", "{{< meta title >}}", "::: div",
    "- item", "# Heading", r"\textbf{x}", "$x^2$", r"\(y\)", "--", "...",
    "'single' \"double\"", "1e-5", "-", "NA", "[1] 2 3", "   leading spaces", "",
]
frame = pd.DataFrame({"text": nasty, "n": range(len(nasty))})
specials = "$%&#_{}~^|*<>@[]`!?=+;:,.'\"-/()\\0123"
frame.index = [f"r{i}{c}" for i, c in enumerate(specials[: len(nasty)])]
frame
```

Column names and a Series:

```{python}
pd.DataFrame([[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]],
             columns=["price ($)", "rate_%", "a|b", "<col>", "#n", r"x\y"])
```

```{python}
pd.Series([1.5, -2.0, 3.25], index=["$a$", "b_c", "<d>"], name="weird & name")
```

`print()` of all of it stays console text:

```{python}
for s in nasty:
    print(s)
```

Printed text that only *looks* like an array, a data frame, an R vector or a
loop table must stay console text:

```{python}
print("[[1 2]\n [3 4]]")
```

```{python}
print("   a  b\n0  1  2\n1  3  4")
```

```{python}
print("[1] 1 2 3")
```

```{python}
print("step 1 cost=0.5\nstep 2 cost=0.4\nstep 3 cost=0.3")
```

```{python}
print("$x$ **not bold** <b>not html</b> {{< meta title >}} \\newpage")
```

A string value displayed (not printed) is its repr:

```{python}
"$x$ & <b>not html</b> 100%"
```
